learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the rules of matching singular and plural subjects with their correct verb forms to write perfect, grammatically correct sentences.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 In a sentence, the Subject and the Verb must always be best friends and agree with each other. If the subject puts on a plural hat, the verb has to match! Let's learn the matching rules! 🤝

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A singular subject (one person/thing) takes a singular verb. A plural subject (more than one) takes a plural verb. The trick? Singular verbs usually end in 's', while plural subjects end in 's'. They trade the 's'!
The pronouns 'I' and 'You' are special rebels! Even though 'I' is singular, and 'You' can be singular, they usually take a PLURAL verb (without an 's').
examples_or_templates: You play the guitar beautifully. (Not 'You plays')

lesson_modules.teaching_content:
Helping verbs must also match the subject!
Singular: is, was, has, does.
Plural: are, were, have, do.
examples_or_templates: She has a pen. / They have pens.
The boy was reading. / The boys were reading.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct verb: 'The birds _____ high in the sky.'
❓ Complete the sentence correctly: 'He _____ not know the answer.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb (play): 'My sister and I _______ chess every evening.'
subjective_practice.hint: 'My sister and I' means 'We'. Is 'We' singular or plural?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the mistake in this sentence: 'A bouquet of flowers are on the table.'
subjective_practice.hint: The subject is 'bouquet' (one bunch), not the flowers inside it!

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Choose 'was' or 'were' for this sentence: 'The leaves on the tree _____ falling.'

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The 'S' Trading Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write 3 singular nouns (dog, star, car) and 3 verbs (bark, shine, zoom). Write sentences making them agree. Notice how if the noun has no 's', the verb gets the 's'! (The dog barks. The stars shine.)

chapter_summary: ⭐ Singular subjects take singular verbs (usually ending in 's').
⭐ Plural subjects take plural verbs (without the 's').
⭐ 'I' and 'You' are exceptions and usually take plural verbs.
